content:
The letters f(x) throw more students than any hard algebra. One learner told me she froze every time she saw them. Then I called f a machine: you feed it a number, it hands one back. She never froze again. That small reframe is the heart of these SAT Math Function Concepts practice questions. Fifteen Digital SAT-style items sit below with instant answers.

Notation is just a recipe

Read f(4) as a command, not a mystery. It says put 4 wherever you see x, then simplify. So if f(x) = 8x + 6, then f(4) = 8×4 + 6 = 38. That is all evaluation ever asks. Practise it until your hand moves before your brain does.

  • f(3) = 7 means the input 3 gives the output 7.
  • Domain is every input the function allows.
  • Range is every output the function can produce.
  • Composition f(g(x)) means work the inside first, then feed the result out.

Domain and range without the fear

Two rules cover almost every SAT case. First, a denominator cannot be zero, so 1/(x−3) bans x = 3. Second, the inside of a square root cannot go negative, so √(x−3) needs x ≥ 3. For range, ask how low or high the output can reach. Since x² and |x| never go below zero, their graphs sit on a clear floor.

You seeAsk thisResult

√(x − 3)What keeps the inside not negative?Domain is x ≥ 3
x² + 5How low can it fall?Range is y ≥ 5

Composition, inside out

Nested functions look scary, yet they follow one order. So compute the inner value first, then hand it to the outer function. For f(g(3)), find g(3), then drop that number into f. Rush it and you invert the order, which flips the whole answer.

Reading functions from a story

The SAT loves context. A tank holds C(t) = 7t + 27 litres after t minutes, so C(7) = 76 simply says 76 litres sit there at minute seven. These SAT Math Function Concepts practice questions include that translation on purpose. Match the number to its unit and the meaning falls out. Watch the two roles carefully. The number inside the brackets is the time, and the value outside is the water. So students who swap them describe the wrong quantity entirely. Read the sentence back in plain English, and the error shows up before you commit to an option.

A caveat worth remembering

f(x) is not f times x. It is one output tied to one input. Students who blur that end up multiplying, and the answer drifts far off. So treat the brackets as a slot, never a multiplication sign.

Tables and graphs say the same thing

The SAT often gives a function as a table or a graph, not a formula. A table row of x and f(x) is just an input paired with its output. So a row where x is 2 and f(x) is 9 tells you f(2) = 9. On a graph, read up from the x-axis, then across to the height of the curve. Both views answer the same question in a different costume. So get comfortable switching between them, since the exam mixes all three forms freely. When a graph looks messy, mark two clean points and trust them. That habit keeps you steady when the formula never appears.

quiz.title: SAT Math Function Concepts Quiz
quiz.intro: Fifteen Digital SAT-style questions on functions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.q: What value of x must be excluded from the domain of f(x) = 1/(x − 3)?
questions.explanation: The denominator cannot be 0: x − 3 = 0 gives x = 3, which is excluded.

questions.q: What is the range of f(x) = |x| + 3?
questions.explanation: Since |x| ≥ 0, the minimum of f is 3, so the range is y ≥ 3.

questions.q: A tank holds C(t) = 7t + 27 liters of water after t minutes. What does C(7) = 76 mean?
options: After 7 minutes the tank holds 76 liters
The tank fills 76 liters each minute
It takes 76 minutes to fill the tank
questions.explanation: C(t) gives liters after t minutes, so C(7) = 76 means 76 liters after 7 minutes.

questions.q: If f(x) = 3x + 7 and g(x) = −x − 1, for what value of x does f(x) = g(x)?
questions.explanation: Set them equal: 3x + 7 = -1x − 1. Then 4x = -8, so x = -2.

questions.q: If f(x) = 3x + 5 and g(x) = 3x², what is f(g(3))?
What is the domain of f(x) = √(x − 3)?
questions.explanation: The expression under a square root must be ≥ 0: x − 3 ≥ 0, so x ≥ 3.

questions.q: What is the range of f(x) = x² + 5?
questions.explanation: Since x² ≥ 0, the smallest value of f is 5, so the range is y ≥ 5.

questions.q: A tank holds C(t) = 4t + 27 liters of water after t minutes. What does C(3) = 39 mean?
options: The tank fills 39 liters each minute
It takes 39 minutes to fill the tank
After 3 minutes the tank holds 39 liters
questions.explanation: C(t) gives liters after t minutes, so C(3) = 39 means 39 liters after 3 minutes.

questions.q: If f(x) = 5x − 4 and g(x) = x + 4, for what value of x does f(x) = g(x)?
questions.explanation: Set them equal: 5x − 4 = 1x + 4. Then 4x = 8, so x = 2.

questions.q: If f(x) = 4x + 2 and g(x) = -2x², what is f(g(-2))?

faq.q: How do I find the domain fast?
faq.a: Hunt for two dangers. A denominator cannot equal zero, and a square root cannot hold a negative. Ban the values that break either rule.

faq.q: Do I need to graph to solve these?
faq.a: Rarely. Most SAT function items yield to substitution and two domain rules. Sketch only when a range or turning point stays unclear.
